name: Warekena do San Miguel
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Ramirez, Henri. 2020. Enciclopedia das linguas Arawak, vol. II, pp. 87-206 (cited on Glottolog as the description covering Warekena do San Miguel)

new_statements.quote: • O acento é contrastivo: émali tucunaré / emáli abiu; kédali rápido / kedáli ressentido; kápisi mão / kapísi quati; ámu fedorento / amú quente; núma faço / numá peço; tátali gavião sp. / tatáli formiga sp.; jálanawi bonito / jalánawi branco. As palavras com mais de um acento são raras e parecem todas do tipo CV́CVCV́. Compare: képelá areia — képela isto é terra. [p.332:] • Em Warekena, não há oposição entre vogais breves e vogais longas.
new_statements.translation: • Accent is contrastive: émali 'peacock bass' / emáli 'abiu fruit'; kédali 'fast' / kedáli 'resentful'; kápisi 'hand' / kapísi 'coati'; ámu 'stinking' / amú 'hot'; núma 'I do' / numá 'I ask'; tátali 'hawk sp.' / tatáli 'ant sp.'; jálanawi 'pretty' / jalánawi 'white'. Words with more than one accent are rare and all seem to be of the type CV́CVCV́. Compare: képelá 'sand' — képela 'this is earth'. [p.332:] • In Warekena there is no opposition between short and long vowels.
new_statements.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas (EDUA). Part II, ch. 4 'Os Warekena', §4.1.3 'Fonologia do Warekena'.
new_statements.locator: printed p. 333 (PDF p. 343), §4.1.3; vowel-length remark printed p. 332
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (130-dpi render of Ramirez 2001, PDF p.343 = printed p.333, header 'LÍNGUAS ARAWAK DA AMAZÔNIA SETENTRIONAL') and the text layer symlink to../bani1255/) lines 13535-13640. The page reads exactly: '• O acento é contrastivo:' followed by a two-column list émali tucunaré | emáli abiu; kédali rápido | kedáli ressentido; kápisi mão | kapísi quati-; ámu fedorento | amú quente; núma faço | numá peço; tátali gavião sp. | tatáli formiga sp.; jálanawi bonito | jalánawi branco; then 'As palavras com mais de um acento são raras e parecem todas do tipo CV́CVCV́. Compare: képelá areia képela isto é terra'. Printed p.332 (txt line ~13605): '• Em Warekena, não há oposição entre vogais breves e vogai…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is lexically contrastive (unpredictable): segmentally identical di- and trisyllables differ only in accent position (initial vs second syllable in all pairs cited); a few CVCVCV words carry two accents (first and last syllable). No positional default rule is stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; only the remark that rare CV́CVCV́ words bear two accents (e.g. képelá 'sand').
new_statements.exceptions: Double-accented CV́CVCV́ words are 'rare'; no other exceptions or rules given. Elsewhere (p.467) Ramirez says the Warekena accent system could not be used for reconstruction 'por falta de dados e de descrições adequadas'.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms (nouns, adjectives, inflected verbs such as núma 'faço'); word-level accent marked with acute; based on the author's own field notes at Guzmán Blanco / río San Miguel. Short sketch (3 pp. of phonology), not an exhaustive analysis; SAPhon's 'Suprasegmental: None' for the same variety contradicts it second-hand.
new_statements.identity_note: Ramirez 2001 ch. 4 describes the Warekena (Walékhena) of the río San Miguel / Guzmán Blanco, Venezuela, from his own field notes — this is Glottolog ware1255 'Warekena do San Miguel / Warekena Velha (Old Warekena)', the language closest to Mandawaka, and NOT Aikhenvald's 1998 'Warekena' of the Xié, which González Ñáñez 2005 and Ramirez 2001:501 identify as Baniva de Maroa/Guainía (guar1293). SAPhon files this same Old Warekena inventory under code gae. Glottolog lists sub-varieties ware1259 (Warekena Velha do Guainía), ware1258 (Warekena Velha do Xié), ware1256 (Cassiquiare); Ramirez's data are from the Guainía/San Miguel speakers (≈ ware1259).

sources.locator: printed p. 333 (PDF p. 343), §4.1.3; vowel-length remark printed p. 332
sources.note: p.333: 'O acento é contrastivo' with seven minimal pairs (émali 'tucunaré' / emáli 'abiu', kédali/kedáli, kápisi/kapísi, ámu/amú, núma/numá, tátali/tatáli, jálanawi/jalánawi); words with more than one accent are rare and all of shape CV́CVCV́ (képelá 'areia' vs képela 'isto é terra'); no vowel-length contrast (p.332). p.467: Warekena accent system left out of the Japurá-Colômbia reconstruction 'por falta de dados e de descrições adequadas'.

sources.citation: SAPhon (South American Phonological Inventory Database), inventory page 'Warekena' (code gae; sources listed: Ramirez 2001; González Ñáñez 2009 Gramática Warekena).
sources.note: Database field 'Suprasegmental: None' (second-hand summary; at odds with Ramirez 2001 p.333 'O acento é contrastivo').

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 1999. The Arawak language family. Ch. 3 of Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds), The Amazonian Languages. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Mentions 'Old Warekena (also called Warena, or Guarequena)' as distinct from Warekena of Xié, but its stress remark (p.79 'Stress is contrastive in some languages (... WX...)') concerns Warekena of Xié; nothing specific on Old Warekena stress.

sources.citation: Ferreira, 2017. Sistemas fonológicos Arawak (Unicamp thesis) — its 'Warekena' (Tabelas 63-64) is Aikhenvald 1998, i.e. Warekena of Xié, not this language.
sources.note: Not applicable to ware1255 (describes the Xié variety); no accent statement for Old Warekena.

sources.note: Wordlist with acute accent marks only (e.g. kápisi 'mão', matching Ramirez); header says 'esperamos incluir um comentário na próxima versão desse dicionário' — no statement on stress.

sources.citation: González Ñáñez, Omar. 2005. Lenguas y nombres de lenguas usados para designar a los pueblos maipure arawakos de la región del Alto Río Negro, Suramérica. Boletín de Lingüística 23: 106-116.
sources.note: Nothing on accent or tone (searched acento/acentua/tono/tonal/prosod: zero hits). Identity paper: Aikhenvald's 1998 'Warekena' of the Xié is Baniva del Guainía; the true Warekena is spoken at Guzmán Blanco and on the río San Miguel (Guainía) and is close to Curripaco.
